lead.hed: Theodore Roosevelt took fuel from Tippecanoe on Oct. 30 while underway in the 7th Fleet
lead.insight: A Navy still released Nov. 1 shows oiler USNS Tippecanoe alongside the carrier on Oct. 30. USNI News, in its Nov. 2 tracker, places Theodore Roosevelt in the South China Sea after Keen Sword 27 ended Thursday. The battle force stands at 286 ships, with 104 deployed and 76 underway. Strike Group 9 includes cruiser Chosin and destroyers Paul Hamilton and Decatur, plus the unmanned surface vessel Seahawk.

political.hed: Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao names Rear Adm. Jonathan Rucker to lead surface shipbuilding
political.insight: USNI News, Wednesday: Cao announced that career submariner Rucker will lead Portfolio Acquisition Executive Maritime, the office created in the department-wide overhaul of how the Navy buys weapons. A Navy release says Rucker has directed design and construction of all submarines since April 2026, and before that was program executive officer for attack submarines and program manager for the Columbia class. He replaces Rear Adm. Casey Moton, acting in the job since August. Submarine buying stays in a separate office, PAE Undersea.

political.hed: Prince of Wales is in the High North as Queen Elizabeth trains off Gibraltar
political.insight: USNI News, Wednesday: Prince of Wales, flagship of the U.K. Carrier Strike Group, took part in a U.S.-led nuclear command and control exercise near Norway. Queen Elizabeth ran deck work with Royal Air Force Chinook helicopters off Gibraltar from Oct. 13 to 26. Prince of Wales is escorted by destroyer Dauntless and Norwegian frigate Fridtjof Nansen under Operation Firecrest. On Oct. 26 the carrier loaded munitions at Hammernesodden, a Norwegian depot that also stores Marine Corps stocks. The ship is headed to Oslo for the Atlantic Future Forum on Nov. 11 and 12.

political.hed: A Marine died Tuesday in a training event at Camp Schwab in Okinawa
political.insight: USNI News, Wednesday: 3rd Marine Division announced the death and is withholding the name until 24 hours after next of kin are told. The Marines are investigating. The division's release says it expresses deepest condolences to the family. Naval Safety Command mishap figures, as reported by USNI, count this as the fourth Marine death in fiscal 2027, three of them in training. The other dates USNI lists are a drowning in Key West on Oct. 3, a death at Quantico on Oct. 30, and an Oct. 8 death after a vehicle rollover.

tech.hed: Saildrone picks a Norwegian yard to build Surveyor drones for northern Europe
tech.insight: Defense News, Wednesday, from the Euronaval show in Paris: the U.S. firm chose Umoe Mandal to produce the Surveyor surveillance craft, with a first mold already being readied. CEO Tom Fidjeland said the work was technically not difficult. Saildrone will supply the autonomy suite, navigation, electronics, and sensors. The Surveyor is 20 meters long, diesel and wind powered, and the company markets it for up to 100 days at sea.

culture.hed: Glasgow's archbishop says half the city's Catholic parishes will close
culture.insight: Stephen Daisley writes in First Things, dated Nov. 3, that falling Mass attendance has hollowed out parishes and that the archdiocese is projected to have just eight priests by mid-century. Archbishop William Nolan announced the shuttering of half the parishes, saying there were too many parishes and too few people. Bellahouston Park has hosted two papal Masses in the past fifty years. Daisley traces the city's Catholic life to Irish immigration in the nineteenth century and to the old Celtic-Rangers split.

culture.hed: Patrick Stewart has died at 86, a Law & Liberty essay says
culture.insight: Titus Techera writes Nov. 4 that Stewart's six-decade career ran from the Royal Shakespeare Company in Stratford-upon-Avon to Hollywood science fiction. His defining role was Captain Jean-Luc Picard in The Next Generation, seven seasons and then four theatrical movies, plus X-Men. The essay's point is the line between lowbrow and highbrow culture in one working life.

culture.hed: An essay says Francis Bacon opened his science project with a prayer for mercy
culture.insight: Algis Valiunas writes in First Things, dated Nov. 4, that Bacon begins The Great Instauration with a petition to the Trinity, asking to endow the human family with new mercies. Bacon insists the inquisition of nature is not the original sin, but closer to Adam naming the creatures. The Fall, Bacon writes, was the desire for moral knowledge so man might revolt from God and give laws to himself. Valiunas says the four centuries since have turned that prospectus into a revolt against divine authority.
